quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If an officer thinks you are driving under the influence, what can you do?

options.text: You can always refuse to be tested.
You can refuse to be tested if it is your first offense.
You cannot refuse to be tested.
You can choose to be tested at a later time.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot refuse to be tested.
questions.explanation: If an officer thinks you are driving under the influence, you must take blood, breath, or urine tests. If you refuse, your license will be revoked.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street?

options.text: When you can clearly see the road ahead.
When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming cars.
When your car is fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street if you can clearly see ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your car can go fast enough to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign if there is no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering the intersection at any stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before you enter and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are octagonal (eight-sided). This shape is used only for stop signs. All eight-sided signs tell you to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn and must go straight.
You still have the right to turn.
You no longer need to turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow pointed. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left because the road is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at the incoming traffic.
Always stay at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid traffic.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: When on a road with two or more lanes, make room for cars entering the freeway. If no one is next to you, move over one lane.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
There may be more pedestrians ahead.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times it is in effect. An "End school zone" sign tells you that the lower speed limit no longer applies.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving. They may include vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones have orange signs with black lettering. Always slow down and pay attention in work zones.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
No right turn.
All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a road is joining from the right ahead.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.
Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.
Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, check that your tires have good tread and are filled to the correct pressure. Slow down when driving in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: If you need to drive in foggy weather:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive at a speed above 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect light back at you and make it harder to see. You must use headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians in the intersection, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the crossing guard's instructions.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow rules that would be in place if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow a crossing guard's directions. Slow down and be extra careful in school zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay in the right lane to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Be sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, make sure the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: When encountering an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Retaliate by tailgating them.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm around aggressive drivers. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make hand gestures. Keep as much distance as possible between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always look behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to see through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop in time. Release the gas pedal first to let your vehicle slow down. Then apply steady brake pressure so your brake lights turn on and your car stops smoothly.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or sirens, drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn.
No stopping.
No U-turn.
Detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may only cross a solid yellow line when you are making a turn.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when there is a gap in traffic.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep tires at the proper air pressure.
Replace tires with bad tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires glide on water between them and the road. Low tire pressure, bad tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: When may you honk your horn?

options.text: When you need to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they plan to turn right. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop for a short time to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive the same as usual.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving. Your mind is focused on your feelings instead of the road. Calm down and get focused before you start driving.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Another driver.
The funeral procession.
A pedestrian.
A bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: The funeral procession.
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. Once the first vehicle enters an intersection, all other vehicles in the procession can follow, even if traffic lights say to stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Shallow water is more dangerous than deep water.
The road gets more slippery as you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less water your tires can push away. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane—sliding on a layer of water.

questions.question: Which factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: The amount of food in your stomach.
Your body weight.
How much time passes between drinks.
All three factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three factors.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent you from getting drunk if you drink too much.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum safe speed for exiting a highway. For example, 30 mph.

questions.question: An oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First honk to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer to the right. Do not steer left—if the other driver swerves at the last second, you will still crash. Brake hard and steadily. Each mile per hour you slow down reduces the crash impact.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against a red light or cross unsafely.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to the same speed as traffic. Signal, check for an opening, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first goes first.
The driver who arrives last goes first.
One driver should drive through without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first goes first.
questions.explanation: All drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to arrive goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, you should:

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found there.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car when stranded in a snowstorm. Rescue workers will find you more easily in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane to maneuver safely. Even though a motorcycle is smaller, it has the same road rights as any other vehicle and needs the full lane width.

questions.question: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to you, you may pass if:

options.text: Only in an emergency.
You are on an expressway.
The road is clear of oncoming traffic.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is clear of oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass. Only pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Drivers may always make U-turns in school zones.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot make a U-turn in a school zone unless no children are present, school is not in session, or signs show school zone rules are not active.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, you should:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your car can cross completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your car can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to cross completely. Never pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children nearby. Before moving, you should:

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and look behind your car before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby. Check that the way is clear before you back up.
